name: DHC-8 Dash 8 (100/200/300)
summary: Canadian high-wing regional turboprop with a T-tail and long nacelles that house the main landing gear, in the earlier, shorter series.

wings: High, straight wing with slight taper
engines: Two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW120-series turboprops in long nacelles
Nacelles extend far behind the wing and house the main landing gear
fuselage: Slender fuselage with a long pointed nose and small oval windows
The -300 is noticeably longer than the -100/-200
Passenger door at the rear left
tail: T-tail with a tall swept fin
Dorsal fillet at the fin root

tellTales: High-wing regional turboprop with a T-tail and very long engine nacelles
Main landing gear folds into the engine nacelles
Long pointed nose and slender fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Q400 is much longer with six-blade propellers and a bigger tail; the 100/200/300 are shorter with three- or four-blade props.
The ATR's landing gear folds into blisters on the fuselage and its nacelles are shorter; the Dash 8's gear folds into the long engine nacelles.
The EMB-120 has a low wing; the Dash 8 has a high wing.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
